land.text: The Illyrian Provinces, 'confirmed' to Austria by the Congress of Vienna (formal annexation 9 June 1815); in 1816 reconstituted as the Kingdom of Illyria without Dalmatia and Croatia but with all Carinthia

successors.note: Austrian troops took the provinces between October 1813 and January 1814.

capitals.name: Laibach (Ljubljana)
capitals.note: Infobox capital Laibach; the military capital was Segna (Senj). Marmont was governor-general from 8 October 1809 to January 1811.

correction.text: Carniola, Gorizia and Gradisca, Trieste, Istria, the Croatian lands southwest of the Sava, western Carinthia and East Tyrol: the Austrian cession of the Treaty of Schonbrunn

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria folds the Illyrian Provinces into its First French Empire shape; the dossier first-french-empire gains them from the Austrian Empire on 14 October 1809). Created 'by the Treaty of Schonbrunn on 14 October 1809' with 'the territories of western (Upper) Carinthia' and Carniola; the Schonbrunn page adds Gorizia and Gradisca, Trieste, the March of Istria and 'the Croatian lands southwest of the river Sava'. The page gives no area; its 1811 population is 1,504,258.

correction.text: The whole of the Illyrian Provinces: the Austrian cession of 1809 plus Dalmatia, Ragusa and Cattaro

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. From June 1810 Dalmatia, Istria and Ragusa are added to the northern provinces: the Kingdom of Italy page, 'Italy lost Istria and the never fully incorporated Dalmatia' (final change effective 10 June 1810); the Illyria page's 15 April 1811 decree divides the whole into four intendancies (Laybach, Karlstadt, Trieste, Zara) and then seven provinces.

correction.text: Ragusa and the Bay of Kotor, the last French garrisons

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. After the Austrian campaign only the Bay of Kotor (to 3 January 1814) and Ragusa (to 27 January 1814) were still French: 'the French garrison surrendered on 27 January 1814, thus effectively ending French rule in the Illyrian Provinces'.

region.text: Carniola, Gorizia and Gradisca, Trieste, Istria, the Croatian lands southwest of the Sava, western Carinthia and East Tyrol: the Austrian cession of the Treaty of Schonbrunn

ledger.note: 14 October 1809: the Illyrian Provinces are created at Schonbrunn. 'the Illyrian Provinces were created by the Treaty of Schönbrunn on 14 October 1809'; Austria ceded 'western (Upper) Carinthia' and Carniola, and (Schonbrunn page) Gorizia and Gradisca, Trieste, the March of Istria and 'the Croatian lands southwest of the river Sava', ending its access to the Adriatic. The Schonbrunn page adds East Tyrol to the Carinthian cession; Marmont became governor-general on 8 October 1809.

region.text: Dalmatia, Ragusa and Cattaro, passed from the Kingdom of Italy

ledger.note: 1810: Dalmatia, Istria and Ragusa pass from the Kingdom of Italy to the Illyrian Provinces. The page: at Schonbrunn Italy 'ceded Istria, Dalmatia and Ragusa to France'; 'The final territorial change came into effect on 10 June 1810' and 'Italy lost Istria and the never fully incorporated Dalmatia'. The page ties 10 June 1810 to the southern Tyrol, so the day is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the northern parts, where Lattermann operated

ledger.note: Autumn 1813: Austria overruns the northern provinces. 'In August 1813, the Austrian Empire again declared war on France'; 'Lattermann operated in northern parts, while Tomassich invaded Dalmatia'. The page names no date for Ljubljana, Carniola, Istria or Croatia; this event bridges that silence, with Trieste (29 October) as the one dated northern fall.

region.text: 'The strategic port of Trieste was taken on 29 October'

ledger.note: 29 October 1813: Austrian troops take Trieste. 'The strategic port of Trieste was taken on 29 October.' The page does not print the year; it follows the August 1813 declaration of war.

region.text: Dalmatia: 'Zara (now called Zadar) surrendered to Austrian and British forces after a 34-day siege on 6 December 1813'; Tomassich invaded Dalmatia

ledger.note: 6 December 1813: Zara surrenders to Austrian and British forces after a 34-day siege. The page dates only Zara; the rest of Dalmatia fell in Tomassich's invasion and its dates are not given, so the region is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the Bay of Kotor, where an insurrection 'aided by Montenegrin forces' and British naval forces besieged Kotor

ledger.counterpart: British naval forces and Montenegrin insurgents
ledger.note: 3 January 1814: the French garrison at Kotor surrenders. 'Arrival of British naval forces led to the siege of Kotor, forcing French garrison to surrender on 3 January 1814.' The Prince-Bishop of Montenegro turned the territory over to Austrian administration on 11 June (1814).

region.text: the region of Dubrovnik (Ragusa), where 'a provisional Ragusan administration was established'

ledger.note: 27 January 1814: the French garrison at Ragusa surrenders. 'the French garrison surrendered on 27 January 1814, thus effectively ending French rule in the Illyrian Provinces' (the infobox reads 1814/1815; the text 1814).

region.text: Ragusa and the Bay of Kotor, the last French garrisons

ledger.note: January 1814: French rule in Illyria ends; Austria holds the provinces until the Congress of Vienna confirms them ('formal annexation by the Austrian Empire: 9 June 1815'), and the Treaty of Paris (30 May 1814) reduced France to its 1792 borders.

wars.name: Austrian campaign in the Illyrian Provinces

union.text: Carniola, Gorizia and Gradisca, Trieste, Istria, the Croatian lands southwest of the Sava, western Carinthia and East Tyrol: the Austrian cession of the Treaty of Schonbrunn
Dalmatia, Ragusa and Cattaro, passed from the Kingdom of Italy

wars.outcome: Austria declared war in August 1813, took Trieste (29 October 1813), Zara (6 December 1813), Kotor (3 January 1814) and Ragusa (27 January 1814), ending French rule; the Congress of Vienna confirmed the provinces to Austria (9 June 1815).
wars.note: The page gives no dates for the northern provinces beyond Trieste.

certainty.note: The Schonbrunn cession names provinces and cities, not a surveyed line; the Military Frontier and the Dalmatian hinterland are approximate, and the 1813 reconquest is dated for only four places.

sources.title: Illyrian Provinces
sources.note: Creation 14 October 1809, capital, 1811 intendancies, the 1813-14 Austrian campaign (Trieste, Zara, Kotor, Ragusa), the Congress of Vienna, the 1816 Kingdom of Illyria.

sources.title: Treaty of Schönbrunn
sources.note: Signed 14 October 1809; the lands Austria ceded to France (Carniola, Istria, Gorizia and Gradisca, Trieste, western Carinthia, Croatian lands SW of the Sava).

sources.title: Kingdom of Italy (Napoleonic)
sources.note: Dalmatia, Istria and Ragusa passing from Italy to the Illyrian Provinces; 10 June 1810; Cattaro and Ragusa 1808.

notes: New dossier, a state Cliopatria lacks: the Napoleonic Illyrian Provinces are drawn inside its 'First French Empire' shape (see first-french-empire, whose ledger already holds the 14 October 1809 gain and the 10 June 1810 Istria and Dalmatia gain). Type 'colony' (an administrative dependency of the Empire, governed by a governor-general). Pages disagree: the Illyrian Provinces page says Napoleon's organization decree was 15 April 1811 (not 1810); the Kingdom of Italy page says Ragusa was annexed in spring 1808 (the Ragusa page's infobox has 31 January 1808, as first-french-empire uses); the Schonbrunn page lists East Tyrol among Austria's cessions to France (East Tyrol and the Hochpustertal were Bavarian from 1805 and went to Illyria in 1810 per the eu-20-g notes; no page opened here dates that, so the 1810 Bavarian transfer is not in the ledger). The northern 1813 fall is confidence 1 (page silent). The Illyria page's table of seven provinces is garbled, so the 1811 provinces are not itemised beyond Carinthia (Villach), Carniola (Laibach), civil Croatia (Karlstadt). Villach and Lienz have no gazetteer place (coordinates used). Not opened for lack of budget: the Kingdom of Illyria (1816) page and the Treaty of Paris (1810).
